text.p: Tele-Communications International Inc chief executive officer Fred Vierra said on Tuesday he does not expect a decision to be made on the company's spin-off from its parent Tele-Communications Inc until mid-year.

"We have filed the necessary documents with the Internal Revenue Service requesting a ruling that the spin-off be a tax free spin," Vierra told Reuters after he gave a speech at the Australasian Cable and Satellite Television conference here.
"I am thinking we will hear something from them around June or July," Vierra said in an interview, adding that TCI chief executive John Malone would then decide on the spin-off plan.

"If the internal revenue says no then as far as spin-off is concerned that would be over, finished, but if they said yes then I think John (Malone), myself and some others will have to decide whether it is in the best interests of the shareholders." Tele-Communications Inc (TCI) is under pressure to lift its lagging financial performance and shore up its share price after several quarters of disappointing results.

"TCI is not in any kind of financial trouble it is just we were trying to do too much at one time," Vierra said. "I think two or three quarters of good strong financial performance and TCI will begin to return to where the market expects it to be."
Vierra said the number one priority for the group was to prepare for the digital age of broadcasting.
He said TCI International had a small investment of about A$1.6 million in troubled Australian satellite TV broadcaster Australis Media Ltd.
"I think we have written that off," he said.
However, Lenfest Communications Inc, 50 percent owned by TCI, has a 32.8 percent economic interest in Australis.
The Australian satellite TV operator suffered a liquidity crisis last year before a finance package with Lenfest and other investors rescued Australis.
Vierra said the TCI group has no plans to expand in the Asia-Pacific region in the near future.
"I think we might use Japan as a stepping stone into Asia, but our investment in Japan is over US$100 million a year at the moment. So we want to watch where our money is going," Vierra said.
TCI has an 82 percent economic interest and voting shares of about 95 percent in TCI International, which operates many of TCI's cable television businesses outside the U.S.
TCI also plans to spin-off Liberty Media Corp as part of its group restructure.
